title: Jervis Demo

series.title: Physical AI Lab: Build a Robot Desk Assistant (4 evenings)

summary: Meet Jervis, Dana's own robot, with everything switched on: every skill, moving eyes and a camera so he can see what's in front of him. A demo stand for events, separate from the four lab evenings.
detail: Jervis is a furry desk robot built the same way as the lab robots, then taken all the way: a Raspberry Pi 5 inside runs this page over Wi-Fi, a Pico moves his mouth, eyes and neck, a USB speaker and mic give him a voice and ears, and a USB camera lets him look. Ask him what he sees, hold something up, or have him read a label. He answers in character, through the Deepgram Voice Agent. This page is the demo setup and the checklist for running him at an event.
outcome: Jervis running on his own: talking, moving his mouth and eyes, using skills, and describing what his camera sees.
artifact: A live robot demo that sees, talks and moves.
prereqs: Jervis: Raspberry Pi 5 on its X1202 battery board, Pico 2 W, BreadVolt, four servos (mouth, neck, two eyes), USB speaker, USB mic and the Hue HD USB camera.
A strong USB-C charger for the X1202 (27 W, 5 V 5 A). A phone charger is not enough for a Pi 5.
The BreadVolt charged before the demo.
A Deepgram API key, and an Anthropic API key for the camera skill. Both are pasted on this page on the robot's own Pi and stay in that browser.

flow.title: Set up Jervis
flow.note: Wiring, power and the checklist before people arrive.

flow.title: Talk to Jervis
flow.note: Open this page on Jervis's Pi. Tick "See with the camera" under Skills, then Start talking.

sections.title: How Jervis is wired
sections.summary: Every wire, so he can be put back together. Hold the Pico with its USB port at the top; pin numbers count from that end.

steps.title: Pi and battery
steps.instruction: The Pi 5 sits on the X1202 battery board (pogo pins, no wires). The USB-C charger plugs into the X1202, not the Pi.
steps.check: The Pi's power light is green.

steps.title: USB into the Pi
steps.instruction: Into the Pi's USB ports: the Pico (micro-USB cable), the Hue HD camera, the USB speaker and the USB mic. Any port works.

steps.title: BreadVolt on the rails
steps.instruction: Push the BreadVolt into the breadboard's power rails: + on the red rail, − on the blue rail. Set its jumpers to 5 V.
steps.check: It sits flat on both rails at 5 V.

steps.title: Ground jumper
steps.instruction: One jumper from Pico pin 23 (GND) to the − rail. Without it the servos have power but can't read the signal.
steps.check: Pin 23 is joined to the − rail.

steps.title: Four servos
steps.instruction: Each servo plug takes three jumpers. Red to the + rail, brown to the − rail, orange to its Pico pin: mouth pin 20 (GP15), neck pin 19 (GP14), left eye pin 17 (GP13), right eye pin 16 (GP12).
steps.check: Every red is on +, every brown on −, every orange on its pin.

steps.title: Nothing on VBUS
steps.instruction: Leave Pico pin 40 (VBUS) empty. A servo there resets the Pico.

steps.title: Charge the BreadVolt
steps.instruction: Plug a USB cable into the BreadVolt's charging port. The red CHG light means it is charging; it goes out when full. A flat BreadVolt is the usual reason the mouth won't move.
steps.check: CHG is off, and PWR lights when you switch it on.

steps.title: Power the Pi
steps.instruction: Plug the X1202's charger into the wall and wait about a minute for the Pi to start. It opens this page on its own.
steps.check: The page is on Jervis's screen.

steps.title: See his screen from a laptop
steps.instruction: On a laptop, go to connect.raspberrypi.com, sign in, and choose Connect via → Screen sharing next to robotfur.
steps.check: You can see and click on Jervis's screen.

steps.title: Connect the Pico
steps.instruction: On the robot page, press Connect robot and pick "Board in FS mode". Do this after every restart. Then press Wiggle the mouth.
steps.check: It says Robot connected and the mouth moves.

steps.title: Switch on the camera
steps.instruction: Under Skills, tick See with the camera and paste the Anthropic key once. The first time, allow the camera when Chromium asks.
steps.check: Ask "what do you see?" and he describes the room.

steps.title: What do you see?
steps.instruction: Hold something up and ask what it is, or ask him to read a label or a sign.
steps.check: He answers from a photo, not a guess.

steps.title: Cross your eyes
steps.instruction: Ask him to cross his eyes, or look left and right.

steps.title: How do I get to the Ferry Building?
steps.instruction: He plans a Muni trip from 505 Howard with live times.
steps.check: He names a line and when the next one comes.

troubleshooting: Mouth doesn't move but the page says Robot connected: the servos have no power. Charge the BreadVolt and switch it on (PWR light), then check the ground jumper from Pico pin 23 to the − rail.
"Low voltage warning" on the Pi, or it keeps restarting: the X1202 isn't getting enough power. Use the 27 W charger, firmly plugged into the X1202.
After a restart the robot page says Not connected: press Connect robot again. The page has to reconnect after every restart.
Pi Connect says robotfur is offline: the Pi is off or still starting. Wait a minute after power-on and refresh.
Jervis says he can't see: check the camera is plugged into the Pi, the camera skill is ticked, the Anthropic key is pasted, and Chromium was allowed to use the camera.
Only one program can use the Pico at a time. Close Thonny or any other tab connected to it.
